data.name: EnergyChartNote
data.value: Average power for each quarter hour that was recorded. A quarter hour the service saw only partly is averaged over the part it saw, so a restart shows as a gap, not as a false dip in production. For {0}, import is above the line and export below; for {1}, charging is above and discharging below. Click a name in the legend to hide that series. A bar along the bottom marks quarter hours that were only partly recorded — the same ones shown in italics in the table below.

data.name: EnergyTableNote
data.value: Every figure is kWh for that interval, in {0} time. Import and export are shown separately, and so are battery charge and discharge: a net figure could not tell a quiet quarter hour from a busy one that happened to balance. {1} is calculated from the other figures (car included), not measured separately.

data.name: NoForecastHeld
data.value: No forecast is available yet. Either no Solcast account is configured, or nothing has been fetched since the controller started — {0} shows which, and is where the account is entered. The forecast is refreshed automatically in daylight; this page shows the last one fetched and never fetches one itself.

data.name: ForecastChartNote
data.value: Expected PV power in 30-minute periods, in {0} time. The line is {1} — the median, equally likely to be beaten or missed. The band behind it is {2}: the wider it is, the less certain the weather. The solid vertical line is midnight between the two days; the dashed one is now. Click a name in the legend to hide that series.

data.name: NoRangeNote_0
data.value: Some periods carry no range of their own

data.name: NoRangeNote
data.value: {0} — the provider sent only a median for them, so the band shrinks to the line there. That does not mean the forecast is certain; the table below shows a dash in those rows.

data.name: MorningMissing
data.value: {0} A forecast provider only forecasts what is still to come, so the controller knows what this morning was expected to bring only if it was running then — and it has nothing saved from before that time. The empty stretch on the left of the chart is missing data, not a morning without sun.

data.name: ForecastTableNote
data.value: Power in W, energy in kWh, times in {0} time. Each row is the half hour it names, and its power is the average the provider expects across that half hour, so the energy column is that power over thirty minutes. Night rows are kept: a 0 W row at 02:00 {1} the forecast, and a table that never drops rows needs no rules to read. A period counts towards the day it {2} on, as on the dashboard and in the day plan, so each day starts with the half hour that ends at its own midnight. {3} — every refresh forecasts them again until the day arrives.

data.name: ForecastHorizonNote
data.value: The forecast covers about 48 hours, so this page shows two days, not a week. The {0} table on the dashboard shows the same two days as four numbers each.
